#1320. Liverpool’s £400m front line clicks but win at Brentford turns on red card

Only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

Admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

But as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

For Andoni Iraola, who had failed to beat Brentford in six attempts as manager of Bournemouth, it would have made for an immensely pleasing sight. After last weekend’s thrashing by Manchester City, Liverpool have responded with a 6-3 Champions League win over LASK and this victory against a previously unbeaten Brentford. Iraola will know, however, that his team’s numerical advantage was the fundamental reason for the dramatic shift in the flow of this game.

The Gtech Community Stadium simmered with outrage following Yarmoliuk’s red card, which came in the eighth minute of first-half stoppage time, and the home fans probably had a point. Yes, there was a movement of the midfielder’s head towards Jacquet, but it was hardly an act of violence. Jacquet’s reaction, collapsing to the turf in mock agony, was embarrassing but predictably effective. Cynics would say the Frenchman changed the game for his team. Purists would argue this is no way in which to influence a match.

Keith Andrews, the Brentford head coach, chose against complaining too aggressively. But he did make it clear what he thought of Jacquet’s behaviour. “I do think they were cute and clever,” Andrews said. “He is walking into Yarmo. But we need to look at ourselves and I understand why it was a red. Yarmo is an amazing young man and he will learn from this.”

Brentford had been the better team before this decisive incident and they deserved their lead, given to them by a majestic header by Keane Lewis-Potter, from Igor Thiago’s cross. It was a moment of attacking quality that Iraola’s glitzy attackers had looked unlikely to replicate, especially when Barcola fluffed a one-versus-one showdown with Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher.

To play an entire half of Premier League football with only 10 men is a brutal examination, though, and Brentford were unable to pass the test. Wirtz unleashed Muñoz after an hour, allowing the Spaniard to fire home with his left foot, before Barcola’s header found Isak in the box with 20 minutes remaining.

It was Isak’s fifth goal of the campaign, which means he has now beaten last season’s tally of four. He has scored in all five of his Premier League appearances against Brentford. “I didn’t have too many chances,” Isak said. “I was waiting for my moment.”

Any hopes of a Brentford comeback evaporated in stoppage time, when the home side lost another man to a red card. This time it was Vitaly Janelt, who received his second yellow for fouling Rio Ngumoha, Liverpool’s sparkling teenage winger. From there, Liverpool’s attempts to score a third were comically poor. “We lacked some composure,” admitted Iraola. “But it was a good battle today, and very important points for us. To take three points here is very valuable.”

An encouraging result for Liverpool, then, but this was not an afternoon without concerns. The first-half showing was worrying, and there were also injuries to Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong. Both players limped off, and Iraola said they will now be out “for some time”.

The loss of Szoboszlai will be a particular concern, as he was rushed back from a hamstring injury for this game but then felt the same muscle again after only 32 minutes of action. “It’s a very delicate situation,” said Iraola.

The injury to Frimpong meant that Muñoz, a winger, played most of the second half as an attack-minded right-back. He did so excellently, and took his goal with impressive composure after Wirtz had pushed the ball into his path. Liverpool’s second was similarly clinical, as Isak pounced on Barcola’s knock-down in a congested penalty area. These, clearly, are the moments of game-changing quality that Liverpool expect from their big-money forwards. Iraola will hope it was a sign of things to come.

Speaking to Sky Sports after his first Premier League win as Fulham head coach, Arbeloa said: “I’m so happy, happy for my players, happy for my supporters, happy for everyone at the club that they deserve this victory. We [waited] a lot of time and some many games that I think we deserved this victory before, but today we did a very good game and yes, I can’t believe that the game finished just 1-0.”

9 - Florian Wirtz's nine chances created from open play against Brentford is the most by a player in a Premier League game since Sadio Mané v Burnley in January 2021 (9) and the most by a player in an away game since Samir Nasri v Spurs in August 2011 (10). Progress. https://t.co/xyMIQP9y5p

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the 3pm kick-offs. Manchester City burst the Anfield bubble last weekend but were defeated by Paris St-Germain in a Champions League thriller on Wednesday, and Enzo Maresca will have to manage his leading cast members’ workload. Before Ipswich Town’s visit to the Etihad he floated the idea of resting some of his players at some point.

“We are thinking about this not just with Erling [Haaland] because we have players, unfortunately or fortunately, they are playing all the games with us and all the games with the international teams,” Maresca said in his pre-match press conference.”

“Elliot [Anderson], Enzo [Fernández], Marc [Guéhi], Erling, Rúben [Dias] – so at some point we probably need to give them some rest.”

Ipswich’s spirited start to the season was characterised by a stunning late turnaround against Fulham last weekend. Gary O’Neil’s side have accrued three wins in their first six top-flight matches for the first time since 1993 and may consider today’s match as something of a free hit.

Elsewhere, Liverpool’s confidence-building midweek win in Austria was underlined by Bradley Barcola’s first, second and third goals for the club. It was exactly what the France winger needed, and with Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo emerging as doubts for this afternoon’s trip to Brentford, the attacking burden may fall on Barcola and Florian Wirtz’s shoulders once more.

Breaking down fourth-placed Brentford, who are one of only three teams to remain undefeated this season, will be a tall task. Keith Andrews’ stock has never been higher, but the same cannot be said for Álvaro Arbeloa, whose winless Fulham are bottom of the league.

Pressure was already mounting before Fulham’s three-game run against the promoted teams, and the late collapse at Portman Road will not have helped the Spaniard’s cause. Defeat by Hull City will not be seen kindly by the club’s hierarchy.

#1319. EURO 2028 qualifying draw: Pots, toughest opponents and ideal group for Italy

The UEFA EURO 2028 qualifying draw will take place on December 6: here’s all you need to know, including the Azzurri’s toughest opponents and their ideal group.

Italy have secured a place among the seeded teams after finishing third in their Nations League group: 54 countries participate in the Euro 2028 qualifying draw, with 24 spots available for the tournament.

There will be five pots: four containing 12 teams each and a fifth with six. Tonight’s matches will determine the final pot allocations.

The draw will result in six groups of five teams and six groups of four. The Azzurri could fall into either category. The 12 group winners and the eight highest-ranked runners-up qualify for EURO 2028.

The other four runners-up and the best-ranked Nations League teams will play for the remaining four spots in the play-offs, but there may be fewer spots available depending on how many host countries qualify.

Teams that qualify for the Nations League semi-finals will be placed in the four-team groups, and those losing in the quarter-finals will go into the five-team groups.

With four Euro 2028 co-hosts, the usual play-off path may change. UEFA could not grant automatic qualification to all four co-hosts, awarding just two spots.

If two hosts qualify through the group stage, the usual format will remain unchanged. If, however, only one qualifies for the tournament, the highest-ranked host nation that failed to qualify will be granted a place, reducing the play-offs to three paths.

If none of the hosts qualify directly, the two highest-ranked will be awarded spots, leaving only two play-off paths to determine the remaining places. However, with England among the co-hosts, this scenario seems highly unlikely.

Italy are in pot 1 alongside Spain, England, France, Belgium, Portugal, the Netherlands, Denmark, Germany, Croatia and Greece, none of which the Azzurri will meet.

The most challenging opponents from Pot 2 seem to be Switzerland, Sweden and Bosnia, not only because each of these three countries has already dealt blows to Italy in recent World Cup qualification campaigns.

Sweden beat the Azzurri in the 2018 World Cup play-off, Switzerland won the qualifying group four years later, and Bosnia beat the Azzurri in the latest World Cup play-off qualifying final this past March.

Slovakia and Scotland seem the toughest opponents from Pot 3.

Gazzetta argues that Italy’s ideal group phase would include Northern Ireland, Romania and San Marino.

Lorenzo Bettoni is the Editor of Football Italia.

#1318. Gerard Pique Issues Statement as Jesus Owono is Given Huge Ban After De Miguel's Death

James is a Senior Editor for GIVEMESPORT with over eight years of experience in the industry. After graduating from the University of Southampton in 2016 with a degree in history, he joined the company as an Academy member in July 2017 and, after a short time working as a freelancer, was given a full-time role in February 2018.  He primarily covers the biggest stories in the football world but is also comfortable reporting on a variety of other sports including darts, golf, Formula 1, tennis, boxing and athletics. He has covered some massive events during his time at GIVEMESPORT, including numerous Champions League and World Cup finals, as well as the Olympics in 2020 and 2024.

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been heavily punished after he was sent off in an incident that led to the death of CD Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.

De Miguel was left fighting for his life after a heavy collision with Owono during the match at Estadio Heliodoro Rodríguez López on November 2.

The Spaniard was rushed to hospital after suffering a blunt cardiac injury on the pitch. He was resuscitated but passed away the following day.

The Disciplinary Committee of the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) have handed Owono a 12-match ban following the incident.

They said in a statement: "The Disciplinary Committee, as an independent body within the federation's structure, has agreed to suspend Jesús Lázaro Ferrer Owono, a player for FC Andorra, for twelve matches for his actions during the CD Tenerife – FC Andorra match. Twelve matches is the maximum penalty allowed by the Disciplinary Code for the events described in the referee's report.

"The referee's report is the only document in the disciplinary proceedings file, and the Committee must determine the sanction based solely on this information. The report describes a violent action, with the leg raised and excessive force used, while the ball was in play. In light of these circumstances, the Committee has determined that the events fall under Article 102 of the Disciplinary Code.

"Furthermore, the subsequent consequences of the action, which are also documented in the referee's report and are public knowledge, have been taken into account to increase the sanction to the maximum level permitted by the regulations. Under no circumstances may the Committee exceed the threshold expressly stipulated in the applicable article."

FC Andorra owner Gerard Pique has now reacted to Owono's ban in an emotional statement. The 39-year-old is adamant that the Equatoguinean did not deserve such a heavy ban.

He said: "This Friday afternoon, we received word that the Committee had handed down a 12-game suspension to Jesús Owono. Let me be clear: Jesús will need more than 12 games before he’s available to play again. No suspension will bring Demi back to us.

"It’s been incredible to see the outpouring of support and affection from all his teammates and family members, and it’s clear that the void he’ll leave behind is enormous. It’s evident that this situation has had a massive impact, not just on Spanish football but worldwide. It’s something completely inexplicable that has never happened before in football, and even now we’re still wondering why.

"Why did this happen? Players, former players, coaches, goalkeepers... they’ve all called it an accident. I truly believe that imposing the maximum penalty on Jesús for this incident puts him in a situation he doesn’t deserve, because he isn’t to blame for any of this. My take on all this is that the 12-game suspension for Jesús Owono seems to me to be placing the blame on Jesús for consequences that weren’t his fault. I believe the penalty should be based on the action itself, not on the consequences."

Pique then referred to an incident in the match between Albacete and Sabadell earlier this month. José Corpas was given a straight red card for kicking Quadri Liameed in the head. Fortunately, Liameed did not suffer a serious injury and Corpas was only given a three-match ban as a result.

He added: "With all this in mind, my reflection is on this: What is being punished, the action or the consequences? I’m making this video because this situation has affected me very deeply on a personal level. First, I was in Tenerife when it happened, and when I went down to the locker room and saw our players’ reaction, I realised that it’s an experience that will stay with all of us who were there for the rest of our lives."

Pique then referred to an incident involving him and former Barcelona goalkeeper Victor Valdes in 2012. In their Champions League semi-final clash against Chelsea, Pique took a blow to the head after colliding with Valdes. He had to leave the pitch and woke up in hospital. Pique said Valdes wasn't to blame and that the situation with Owono was very similar.

He finished: "And we humans often need to blame someone because, otherwise, we can't understand why this happens on the field. It's an accident. I think imposing the maximum penalty on Jesús puts him in an unfair situation, because he isn't to blame for what ended up happening."

Tenerfie manager Alvaro Cervera disagrees with Pique, saying Owono's ban may seem light, but that the rules don't allow for anything else.

Owono, meanwhile, is said to be distraught following De Miguel's death. It was revealed last week that he wanted to reach out to De Miguel’s family in order to ‘share in their grief and offer his condolences in person’. It is unknown when he will return to football, if at all.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

After four years of enjoying an upward trajectory under Eddie Howe, the team faded last season, sold their best players in the summer, lost the manager and there is no evidence yet they have replaced anything with better.

This was supposed to be a reaction to the embarrassing 4-1 thrashing at Coventry City, but it led to another loss and, in the first half at least, another abject display. It is in danger of resembling a shell suit that has emerged from the back of the wardrobe for a Saturday night out.

There is so much confidence in the German in the Newcastle boardroom that they believe improvement is inevitable, but that is far from assured. Juventus have shared a video of Kenan Yildiz training on the pitch, with the caption: ‘One step at a time, Kenan.’

#1315. What’s Happened to Chido Obi Since He Joined Willem II as Man Utd Consider Action

James is a Senior Editor for GIVEMESPORT with over eight years of experience in the industry. After graduating from the University of Southampton in 2016 with a degree in history, he joined the company as an Academy member in July 2017 and, after a short time working as a freelancer, was given a full-time role in February 2018.  He primarily covers the biggest stories in the football world but is also comfortable reporting on a variety of other sports including darts, golf, Formula 1, tennis, boxing and athletics. He has covered some massive events during his time at GIVEMESPORT, including numerous Champions League and World Cup finals, as well as the Olympics in 2020 and 2024.

Manchester United have several talented youngsters in their ranks at the moment, but arguably the best of the bunch is Chido Obi.

The Danish striker hit the headlines in 2023 when he scored 10 goals for Arsenal in an under-16 match against Liverpool. Obi decided that Arsenal wasn't the best team to continue his development, though, and he signed for Man Utd in the summer of 2024.

The youngster was just 17 years old when he made his debut for the Red Devils. He went onto play eight times for the first-team in the 2024/25 campaign as he looked to make his mark in the Premier League.

After failing to make a single appearance in 2025/26, Obi joined Eredivisie outfit Willem II on a season-long loan in September. United would have hoped that he could continue his development in the Netherlands and return a much better player, but things haven't worked out as they would have hoped.

Three days after signing for Willem II, Obi made his debut for the club against Excelsior. He played the final eight minutes as Willem II were beaten 3-0.

A few weeks later, he made his home debut for the club, coming on as a late substitute in a 5-1 defeat to Dutch giants Ajax. Obi put in a promising performance as he played a key role in his side's goal. He has failed to kick on from there, though.

It's been a dismal campaign so far for Willem II, who are still waiting for their first win in the Eredivisie. They are currently rock bottom of the Netherlands' top tier, having picked up just three points from their opening 12 matches. They are seven points away from safety.

Despite Willem II's struggles, Obi has struggled for game-time. He has not started a single game for the club, coming on as a second-half substitute on six occasions. He has not found the back of the net in the 71 minutes he has played.

He was given 24 minutes in his side's victory over Helmond in the Dutch Cup on October 27. After the match, caretaker boss Adrie Koster wasn't happy with his defensive efforts when Willem went down to ten men.

Koster said: "It is partly a matter of mindset, but also of youthful exuberance. That boy has never experienced anything like this before. He doesn't do it on purpose either, so we shouldn't focus everything on him. This is simply part of his learning process. But we are going to talk to him about it."

Obi's struggles have been so great that United are said to be considering recalling him in January. The Manchester Evening News report that United insert break clauses into the contracts of each young player they send on loan, and that they will consider activating the clause if Obi's situation does not improve.

Still only 18 years old, Obi still has time to fulfill his lofty potential. His spell in the Netherlands has been nothing short of a nightmare so far, though. It remains to be seen whether he can turn his fortunes around.

#1314. Mauricio Pochettino swaps one football for another as new Man United boss continues US farewell tour at NFL clash ahead of final game in charge

By ISABEL BALDWIN, US ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 22:54 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 22:55 EST, 15 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino's United States farewell tour continued on Sunday night with a pitstop at an NFL showdown.

The manager has one game left in charge of the United States before parting ways with the national team to join Manchester United after agreeing a deal with the Premier League club earlier this week.

The Argentine will replace Michael Carrick at Old Trafford on a two-and-a-half year contract after United agreed to pay more than £10million ($13m) to buy him and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

Before his return to England, the 54-year-old is enjoying his swansong with the US. In between overseeing his final games in charge of the national team, Pochettino was spotted soaking in the action of the other variety of football.

The former Tottenham Hotspur boss attended the primetime NFL showdown between the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio on Sunday night.

The head coach, sporting his blue USSF coat, was captured standing on the sidelines with members of his staff ahead of the Sunday Night Football matchup.

USMNT and future Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is at the Bengals-Steelers game 😭🇺🇸 pic.twitter.com/B7Irn0YLnd

Mauricio Pochettino's United States farewell tour continued at the NFL on Sunday night

The new Manchester United boss attended the Cincinnati Bengals' game at Paycor Stadium

He was greeted by kicker Evan McPherson, long snapper William Wagner and punter Ryan Rehkow - members of the Bengals' special teams - on the turf before kickoff.

The US is set to face Haiti in the second-leg of their CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinal at TQL Stadium in Cincinnati on Tuesday.

The game, which will take place around a mile north of the Bengals' Paycor Stadium, will mark Pochettino's final match in charge of the US national team.

He also took charge of the USA's 6-0 first-leg win against Haiti on Tuesday, which marked the first stop on his farewell tour.

Pochettino will begin his new role with Manchester United on Wednesday, immediately following Tuesday's second-leg. His first game will be against Liverpool at Anfield next Sunday.

He emotionally addressed his departure from the US setup and impending new job in a press conference on Friday.

Flanked by US Soccer Federation bosses at the team’s headquarters in Georgia, an emotional Pochettino wiped away tears as he thanked the players and staff.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he said. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

The Argentine was captured on the sidelines ahead of the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers

‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay.

‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'

#1313. Pierre Sage fears for his Crystal Palace future after Brighton humiliation

Pierre Sage has admitted that he fears for his future at Crystal Palace, adding that he felt “shame” after his side slumped to their joint-heaviest defeat by rivals Brighton and Hove Albion.

Sage replaced Oliver Glasner as manager in June but since then Palace have won just two league matches with him in at the helm. The south London club have taken seven points from seven Premier League games and have already conceded 17 goals, the most of any team in the league.

“I don’t know,” Sage said when asked if he will get enough time to rectify Palace’s slump. He admitted that his shame was about how Palace were overwhelmed, leaking three goals within the first nine minutes of the game before eventually losing 5-0.

“We are not at the level we expected, and I’m really sorry for that,” the 47-year-old said. “I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face.”

The Frenchman said that he took full responsibility for the 5-0 defeat, and understood why hundreds of Palace fans left well before the final whistle.

“I cannot blame anybody because we didn’t do the job in a good way,” he said. “I’m responsible for this team, and when the team play as today, it’s not normal. It’s my fault. I understand them.

“Another feeling is about shame because that’s my feeling after the game and from the beginning. It’s not normal to not respect the necessary of this kind of game.”

Sage admitted that he will be assessing how Palace need to rethink their approach in the coming fixtures, beginning with Thursday’s trip to Besiktas in the Europa League.

“The first work to do is on me,” he said. “I’m responsible for what’s happened on the pitch, and I have a lot of work to do because I have to change this kind of thing.

“It’s maybe in the preparation, in the way we give them the motivation to start the game just before in the locker room in the warm-up. We have to analyse that because it’s not normal. And today it was really at the highest level we cannot expect, and that’s the moment to change the thing.”

For all the scrutiny on his back three, Sage urged his entire side to take greater defensive responsibility, highlighting how the team were too passive in pressing Brighton. Palace have struggled to regain the solidity that long characterised the side since the departures of Marc Guéhi in January and Maxence Lacroix this summer.

“The way of defending is not only on the back three; it is for every player, and there are some things to do collectively, too,” Sage said. “When we defend low we struggle a lot.”

Sage joined Palace after a fine campaign with Lens. He led the club to second place in Ligue 1, just six points off Paris St-Germain, and victory in the Coupe de France. Yet, despite Sage’s reputation when he moved to Selhurst Park, his suitability for the Palace job is increasingly being questioned.

Three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Sage could suffer the same fate, with doubts growing that he will still be in charge for Thursday’s trip to Besiktas.

“It’s not my decision,” Sage said. “I don’t want to accept the level of the moment if we are able to do better. And today the work is really important to do, and I will do it. It’s my job, and I’d like to change this.”

With only Manchester City and Arsenal above them, Brighton and Hove Albion are entitled to dream of making history. Yet, whatever happens between now and May, one accolade is already surely their own: the goal of the season award.

Diego Gómez’s 56-yard strike will instantly become the stuff of Brighton lore. The Paraguayan’s audacity will be even more cherished for coming against Crystal Palace, who were pummelled 5-0 in the M23 derby.

All Premier League defeats are equal but some are more equal than others. Three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Pierre Sage is at grave risk of suffering the same fate. Naturally, Brighton fans revelled in reminding him of this threat as the final whistle approached.Palace were so ragged that their performance felt like a defeat that marks the end of a managerial reign. Even stand-in captain Adam Wharton was guilty of dawdling and losing the ball in possession. Hundreds of away supporters left well before the full-time whistle and those who remained booed all players bar Jefferson Lerma.

With less venom in attack, especially with Ismaïla Sarr being an unused substitute, Palace’s sole chance lay in counter-attacking. This strategy disintegrated in the fourth minute, when Jaydee Canvot headed Pascal Gross’s free-kick into his own net.

Jaydee Canvot glances the ball into his own net and Brighton lead! 🔵 https://t.co/subm9ggwId

But the hint of self-immolation in Palace’s display should not obscure the swagger of Brighton’s performance. Despite losing Danny Welbeck, last year’s top scorer, Brighton have scored 23 goals already this Premier League campaign, the most in the league. This tally includes one of the most extraordinary goals in Premier League history.

Most simply, Gómez’s goal, which put Brighton 2-0 up in the seventh minute, was a triumph of the imagination. Receiving a short pass from Olivier Boscagli just inside his own half, Gómez could have sought to pick out a team-mate. Instead, his scanning of the pitch before receiving the ball had revealed that goalkeeper Walter Benítez was off his line and Brighton’s attacking players were being tightly guarded by defenders. And so, just as he entered the centre circle in the opposition half, Gómez attempted the absurd.

“I’m not training with Diego Gómez shooting from 50 metres in training,” head coach Fabian Hürzeler said while breaking into a smile. “It’s just about making the players quick in their minds.

The presence of mind to attempt something outlandish was one thing; the execution was quite another. With Benítez vulnerable, Gómez took just one touch with his right foot before taking his shot, not giving the keeper enough time to scramble back to cover his line. All that remained was for the Paraguayan international to hurtle towards the corner flag, engulfed by his ecstatic team-mates. For the Brighton fans, soaked by showers at the Amex, rain can never have felt so sweet.

Gómez’s goal will earn comparisons with David Beckham’s lob from the halfway line at Wimbledon. The advancements in pressing and conditioning in the 30 years since, with space ever more congested, makes such a strike even harder today. Not since Wayne Rooney in 2017 has a player scored a Premier League goal from further out than Gómez’s 56 yards.

Gómez may well attempt an encore. He shot from even further out at the Stadium of Light a week ago. When October ends, three of the last four Premier League goal-of-the-month winners will be Brighton players. Alongside his meticulous emphasis on set-pieces, Hürzeler empowers flair in open play.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the M23 derby – or El Gatwicko, as the kids call it these days – as high-flying Brighton and Hove Albion host Crystal Palace at the Amex Stadium. Being frank, this is neither the fiercest nor the most storied Premier League rivalry, but few would have imagined when these sides faced off in the Third Division in the mid-1970s that this would ever become a top-flight match-up sandwiched between European games.

Brighton have been outstanding this season and took their league form into the Conference League, thrashing Lithuanian champions Kauno Zalgiris on Thursday night. Fabian Hürzeler was delighted by his fringe players’ performances on Thursday night and may have some selection questions to answer with Jack Hinshelwood and Georginio Rutter finding the net. Brighton are third in the Premier League and were the division’s heaviest scorers after the last round of matches.

Yet the Palace nut has been a tough one to crack for Hürzeler, having not yet registered a win in four attempts. When asked what he enjoyed most about the rivalry, the German said: “Nothing yet, because I didn’t win any games so far. Hopefully on Sunday this changes… I like these games because they’re derbies, more emotions, it’s a rivalry, it’s [us] against Crystal Palace.”

In his pre-match interview Hürzeler admitted to being an admirer of Pierre Sage, and while the Frenchman’s side have failed to match Brighton’s fast start, they rallied impressively to defeat rivals Nottingham Forest last weekend and fought back valiantly away at Lyon, albeit in a losing effort, in midweek. The return of Ismaïla Sarr from injury is a significant boost.

Elsewhere Bournemouth host Sunderland hoping to secure their first Premier League victory of the season. Marco Rose’s side and Tottenham are the only teams still without a win, but Bournemouth have been perfect in the Europa League and will look to transfer some of that momentum into the league. Sunderland scored late to win away at Portuguese side Torreense.

#1312. Efficient catalyst-controlled C–H arylation of arenes

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

We’re sharing this article early to provide faster access to peer-reviewed, accepted research. It is citable and carries a permanent DOI. This version is subject to further edits and will be replaced automatically by the final Version of Record. All legal disclaimers apply.

Direct arylation of C–H bonds in arenes offers a streamlined alternative to widely used cross-coupling reactions.1 However, native substrates lack the preinstalled functional handles that ordinarily provide both reactivity and control over the site of reaction. Consequently, despite long-standing interest in directly engaging C–H bonds as reactive sites,2–4 the design of general catalysts that deliver high yields across diverse substrate classes while controlling site selectivity remains a challenge.5–12 Here we show that a microenvironment around a prototypical palladium dicarboxylate catalytic site can provide high selectivity for direct arylation of sterically exposed C–H sites, while high efficiency is achieved using an advanced palladium(II) precatalyst and tailored diaryliodonium reagents for selective aryl transfer. The applicability of this system spans from electron-rich to electron-deficient arenes, while electron-neutral benzene, which is often a challenge for C–H arylation, undergoes successive sterically controlled arylations, delivering functionalized polyaryl compounds. In addition to removing the necessity for pre-functionalized substrates, the mild conditions enable direct late-stage C–H arylation and the installation of aryl groups equipped with functionalities that are typically either reactive in traditional cross-coupling catalysis, such as triflates, iodides, and boronate esters, or sensitive to the basic conditions, such as N-hydroxysuccinimide esters. The results emphasize the distinct synthetic value of palladium-catalyzed direct C–H arylation reactions and showcase a catalyst platform that facilitates high yields and control over site-selectivity.

#1311. All 92 English Clubs Ranked By Average Attendance For the 2026/27 Season

All 92 English football clubs, from League Two to the Championship and Premier League, have been ranked by their average attendances for the 2026/27 season so far.

The results make for a fascinating read. While some of England's biggest clubs, including Manchester United, Liverpool and Arsenal, unsurprisingly find themselves near the top, there are certainly a few curveballs along the way.

Some clubs boasting the biggest stadiums haven't necessarily managed to pack out their impressive arenas, while a number of typically 'smaller' sides (for want of a better word) have punched above their weight and ranked higher than expected, thanks in part to their flying starts to the campaign.

Ranking at the very bottom, with an average attendance of just 1,853, are Accrington Stanley. The club's main claim to fame remains their 1989 milk advert, in which a child famously asks, “Accrington Stanley, who are they?” They rank as one of the smallest clubs in the country, but have to be given some sort of let-off for their close proximity to Manchester and Liverpool.

Barnet, Fleetwood Town - who recently knocked Arsenal out of the League Cup - and Salford City, rank just above them, with the latter being owned by some of Man United's Class of 92 but still struggling to find their own identity. This comes despite sitting top of League Two and among the favourites for another promotion.

Other notable clubs who feature in this section are Grimsby Town in 72nd, who own one of the ugliest stadiums in British football, while Swindon Town - who found themselves in the topflight in the 1993/94 season - rank two places ahead, with the Robins managing just 7,608 fans at their games this season.

English football's top-flight is one of the most closely-followed leagues in the world.

Oldham Athletic, York City and Blackpool are among several clubs in this section that have struggled to stay afloat in recent years, with all three coming perilously close to extinction because of financial troubles. Part of the problem may stem from the fact that none regularly attract more than 10,000 fans to home matches, although the wider state of the English game is a far bigger factor.

Despite enjoying three successive promotions over the last three seasons as they set their sights on reaching the Premier League sooner rather than later, Wrexham still have around 200 empty seats per match at present. They rank 54th on this list, behind the likes of Barnsley, Lincoln City and MK Dons.

Bournemouth's rise to prominence followed a similar path to Wrexham's, but they have yet to move away from their old, much smaller stadium. As a result, they boast the lowest average attendance of any Premier League side, ranking 51st overall, just one place above Luton Town, who have endured successive relegations in the opposite direction.

Brentford, who have to contend with the fact that several of their London neighbours boast much bigger fanbases, sit 42nd, behind Watford, Swansea City and Huddersfield Town.

Millwall, meanwhile, are renowned as one of the toughest clubs in English football and, alongside south London rivals Charlton Athletic, find themselves averaging just under 20,000 fans at home matches. It's a similar story for two-time FA Cup winners Portsmouth. Another side with a reputation for making plenty of noise are Stoke City, who average 22,288 in the Championship. That figure just about keeps the age-old question of 'can he do it on a cold, wet Tuesday night in Stoke?' alive and kicking.

The most incredible football stadiums on the planet - ranked in order.

Other top-flight sides in this section include Hull City in 29th, Crystal Palace in 27th and Fulham in 22nd. None of them quite manage to attract more supporters than Leicester City, however, despite the Foxes sitting 10th in the division below.

The three biggest clubs missing out on a place in the top 10 are Nottingham Forest (16th), Leeds United (13th), and Aston Villa (11th). But there is quite a jump between them and Chelsea, who just about make it in 10th with an average attendance at Stamford Bridge of 39,507.

Arsenal, top of the league as they look to retain their first Premier League title in 22 years, are surprisingly only sixth, behind both Manchester City and Liverpool. This means they also rank third in London, with Tottenham in third and West Ham in second.

But there's no surprise that Manchester United's Old Trafford, the biggest club stadium in the UK, ranks top. Fanbanter's findings suggest their attendance has increased from last term, despite the Red Devils having recently sacked Michael Carrick for Mauricio Pochettino as they sit 18th and in the relegation zone.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#1310. Report Napoli reject PSV bid for De Bruyne

Dutch newspaper De Telegraaf reports that Napoli have rejected an opening bid from PSV Eindhoven for Kevin De Bruyne worth €2m.

Napoli have reportedly rejected an opening offer for their midfielder De Bruyne.

According to De Telegraaf, the Partenopei have turned down a €2m bid from Dutch side PSV, who have already opened talks with the ex-Manchester City star.

De Bruyne’s contract at the Stadio Maradona expires at the end of the season, and the midfielder has recently refused to rule out a possible January switch to PSV.

According to the report, De Bruyne is open to moving to PSV in the January window, which would allow him and his family to move into the home they own in the Belgian Limburg.

It is still unclear whether Napoli will be open to selling the experienced midfielder in January.

According to De Telegraaf, the Partenopei will ask for a higher transfer fee, while Corriere dello Sport claims the Serie A side wants to retain De Bruyne until the end of the season.

Napoli hold an option to extend De Bruyne’s contract until 2028, while Gazzetta reports that Frank Zambo-Anguissa, rather than the Belgian, could leave in January, with Marseille interested in the Cameroonian midfielder.

#1309. Slow and dull Man Utd are just not good enough

Manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet. You fix one problem – being far too vulnerable to conceding goals – only to create another – lacking the threat to score. It is all very Meh United not Man United. The indisputable fact is they are just not very entertaining to watch. They are slow and dull.

In the end it also points to another thing. The thing highlighted in midweek by Lisandro Martínez after the Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid: they do not have the strength in depth to compete.

What they do have appears to not be fit for purpose. Certainly Michael Carrick, the under-pressure manager, is struggling to get the best out of the resources he has.

“It’s like a duvet,” Toshack, the former Real Madrid and Wales manager, famously said of football. “If you pull it up, your feet get cold. If you pull it down, your shoulders get cold.”

There will have been times in the last few days, with the intense criticism and scrutiny over his future, when Carrick will have simply felt like dragging that duvet up over his head and keeping it there.

Defeat by Leeds United would have been unthinkable. It would have put Carrick under potentially intolerable pressure in what appears to be a pivotal week, with Como away in the Champions League and a home Premier League fixture against Bournemouth in the coming days.

Was this a lifeline or the tightening of the noose for Carrick? Time will soon tell. The relief of avoiding defeat was tempered by the reality of it now being just one win in their opening seven league games – at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town – and they are down in 13th place. It is six games without a win in all competitions.

That is unacceptable and is their fewest number of league victories in a top-flight campaign since 1986-87. Back then they sacked their manager in November and brought in a certain Alex Ferguson.

The hard truth is Carrick needs to start collecting some “Ws” in those results columns. United are already 14 points behind leaders Manchester City and five outside the probable Champions League places. Qualifying again for that tournament must be the minimum expectation.

Ruben Amorim, Carrick’s predecessor, lost his job within 24 hours of the same 1-1 scoreline at Elland Road last season – dismissed after Martínez-like explosive comments again aimed at director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick will not suffer the same fate after this, but the ice is becoming increasingly thin.

We have seen this movie before at United. A slow start to the season, a period of drift, falling out of contention, no reaction on the pitch, backing from the hierarchy that becomes increasingly unconvincing. And then a change.

Can Carrick, who genuinely does still retain support at the highest level, alter that pattern? Does he have it in him? Is he too passive like his team? Carrick said this draw felt like a “fresh start”, but on this evidence that comment can be classified as wildly optimistic.

Having directed his criticism at the United hierarchy, and specifically Wilcox, the former Leeds winger who was here, over a lack of summer signings, Martínez apologised and was named in the starting XI. But the Argentine only lasted to half-time, withdrawn injured with a tight thigh, and sat watching the second half with his hood up over his head.

What United did sign in the last window was three midfielders – at a cost of £155m – and all three started: Carlos Baleba alongside Andrey Santos with Youri Tielemans in the No 10 role, which meant Bruno Fernandes was pushed out to the left, from where he constantly wanted to come in-field, with Amad Diallo on the right.

Carrick talked of having a “fresh spine” as well as that fresh start. But it did not make for a potent combination even if, further forward, Bryan Mbeumo played through the middle and scored one. He should have scored another.

Bryan Mbeumo finds the net this time to put Manchester United 1-0 up at Leeds! 🔴 https://t.co/NKDIhlUND1

But beyond that United created little. “It was a dominant performance against Man United,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, claimed. He was right. If one team deserved to win it was his. They had the chances but snatched at them with Anton Stach, in injury time, having a weak shot cleared off the line by Martínez’s replacement Noussair Mazraoui after a mistake by goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Stach had to score.

United were ahead at half-time. Mbeumo had headed wastefully wide when unmarked but did well to force his way past James Justin and meet a low cross from Tielemans to poke the ball home. The way the usually undemonstrative Carrick punched the air in his technical area showed the pressure he felt. It was something to build on. To gain control.

Leeds had started well but did not really pose much of a threat – beyond forcing Lammens to save well from Nico Elvedi’s downward header – and maybe the earlier kick-off subdued the crowd. This was far from a bear pit.

But after the break, Leeds were comfortably the better side. The nature of their equalising goal, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin too strong and alert for first Baleba and then Mbeumo to fire in from a corner, exposed the enduring softness at the heart of United.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalises for Leeds against Manchester United 👊 https://t.co/mnpyxZJKbm

And that must be addressed by Carrick, especially as he appeared to sacrifice attacking intent by shoring up defensively. But that duvet is looking far too inadequate right now. Or Carrick is making it appear so.

Michael Carrick says he has put on “the headphones” this week in an effort to drown out the noise, but admitted Manchester United have to stop their struggles from snowballing.

United sit just two points above the relegation zone after a 1-1 draw at Leeds left them with just one win from their opening seven Premier League matches.

Carrick claimed the result felt like a “fresh start” after a week in which Lisandro Martínez publicly apologised for criticising Jason Wilcox, the United director of football, and the Old Trafford board.

But the United manager acknowledged their position “doesn’t look too good” and that they must start winning soon to stop the club from entering another doom cycle.

“Listen, we’re not accepting it as everything’s great by any stretch, so I’m realistic with that,” said the United manager, who claimed “the headphones have been on this week”.

“But sometimes you do struggle, sometimes there’s a bit of it where you have to find a way through it. We haven’t really had to go through that yet [before now] and we have to find a way through it.

“There has been a cycle at times here over a period of time when it can go in different directions. We’ve got to be stable enough to keep doing the right things for the right reasons as a group, and we’re more than capable of winning football matches.

“I understand the situation doesn’t look too good if you look at it from a certain way, but I’ve no doubts we can go on a good run.”

United face Como in the Champions League in Italy on Wednesday before Bournemouth visit Old Trafford four days later.

Carrick said he remains convinced United can still have a strong campaign, despite their worst start to a season for 40 years. I know what we’ve got in the changing room, where we want to get to, how we want to get there,” he said. “We know we can do it.

“We’ve done it for some time, and we feel we’re a better group now, and I do feel that. Sometimes it doesn’t always show, but you get a feeling and I’m encouraged by a lot of things. And if we keep doing the right things, I think we can still have a really good season.”

Asked if he would be putting the headphones back on this week ahead of two more pivotal games, Carrick added: “Nah, it’s always quiet for me.”

Martínez was substituted at half-time at Elland Road with a tight thigh just days after his tirade at club executives and Marcus Rashford was left out for “purely tactical” reasons. “Nothing personal, the front players were doing a good job on and off the ball,” Carrick said. “Everyone is ready for Wednesday.”

The Leeds boss told Sky Sports: “We are slightly disappointed it is just a point. Overall, I felt it was not necessary to be losing at half time but it is still Manchester United. Second half, we got the equaliser, we should have kept up the dominance, too many strikes went over the crossbar but it was overall a solid performance. We should have won the game but we move on.

“We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month if we were seen as favourites against Manchester Untiedbut we have earned this. We wanted to prove the comments right.

“We were the dominant side but we couldn’t capitalise as we lacked quality in and around the box.

“It says a lot about how much respect we have earned. Overall, this is where we are at the moment and overall, it is a good place to be.

“It is still difficult in this league to win points. You have to be clinical and be very, very effective but we have to keep going.”

Speaking to Sky Sports, he said: “I think we could’ve played with a bit more quality in the final third, particularly in the first half. We were getting good quality in the box but just not enough numbers.

“We made sure in the second half we came out with more confidence going forward. I think we were unlucky not to win the game.

“They tried to [match us up formation-wise]. Not surprised given what happened last season. They were probably looking at our physical output and the way we liked to play and tried to go man-for-man.

“It took us a little bit to adjust to it, but I don’t think it was too difficult to adjust. It was more down to us and maybe a lack of quality in the final third.”

#1308. Hey, Jude! England's star man Bellingham gets celebratory kiss from girlfriend Ashlyn Castro in a rare public appearance together after he led the Three Lions to beating world champions Spain

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 03:53 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 04:20 EST, 16 November 2026

Jude Bellingham sealed England's stunning 3-2 victory over world champions Spain with a kiss from girlfriend Ashlyn Castro as the couple made a rare public appearance together on Sunday.

England, who romped to a 3-0 lead with a superb display before the hour mark, were forced to weather a late onslaught from the Spanish after Elliot Anderson was shown a red card in the 63rd minute of the Nations League clash.

Although Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams managed to claw two back for this year's World Cup winners, England held on with a backs-to-the-wall effort in the closing stages, courtesy of a few fine saves from Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford.

After England's victory, which called an end to Spain's historic 43-game unbeaten run, Bellingham was spotted celebrating with his model girlfriend Ashlyn inside the stadium.

Wearing a beaming smile, he went over to embrace both the 28-year-old American and his father Mark as the family soaked up the celebrations in the stands.

The Real Madrid superstar has largely kept his relationship with Ashlyn private since the pair were first linked in early 2025.

Jude Bellingham and his girlfriend Ashlyn Castro celebrate England's superb win over Spain

The Real Madrid star then caught up with his dad Mark on a special night for the Bellinghams

Ashlyn is a model and social media influencer from California (@instagram/ashlyncastro)

Ashlyn is a model and social media influencer from California who boasts over one million followers on Instagram, sharing fashion and beauty content online.

Spanish media waxed lyrical about Bellingham's display on the night, claiming he was 'determined to make a statement' at the stadium of Real Madrid's rivals Atletico.

Newspaper AS wrote: 'If anyone felt the match was crucial, it was Jude Bellingham. He stepped onto the Metropolitano pitch determined to make a statement, to impose his usual footballing and physical prowess.

'He exudes football in every movement, and his rise to the top is unstoppable.'

It was a proud international break for the Bellinghams before a ball was kicked in Madrid, with Jude's 21-year-old younger brother Jobe also earning his first England call-up last week.

Jude and Jobe would have become the first brothers to play for England since Gary and Phil Neville 17 years ago, but the younger sibling stayed on Thomas Tuchel's bench as an unused substitute.

England, who topped Group C on goal difference over Spain, will now not play until the Nations League quarter-finals kick off next spring.

The final, should Tuchel's Three Lions make it that far, are scheduled for the summer.

#1307. Fabrizio Romano: Joshua Zirkzee to Hold Talks With Pochettino Over Man Utd Exit

Manchester United are already planning for the January transfer window under Mauricio Pochettino before he has even officially taken charge.

The Red Devils have appointed the Argentine to replace Michael Carrick as their manager on a two-and-a-half-year deal until 2029, having won just one of their opening 10 games in the Premier League, which has left them 18th in the table.

Pochettino is scheduled to take over on November 18th officially, with his first game in charge coming just days later against arch-rivals Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday afternoon. But the decisions over who will be in his squad in the long-term have already begun.

Fabrizio Romano shared an update last week that stated the 54-year-old has already hold talks with the club's hierarchy over plans for the winter window, with the board expected to provide funds for him to strengthen his squad.

A left-back and a striker are believed to be the top priorities, and now speaking in his latest video on YouTube, Romano revealed that there are also conversations planned between the new gaffer and current players in the squad to discuss their future, including Joshua Zirkzee.

"Man United, in any case, want to try to get another striker in the January transfer window," he said.

"Could be an opportunity on loan, or could be a striker who can also be for the long term, depending on the opportunities, depending on the finances. But obviously, to understand the future of Joshua Zirkzee is also very important to get to the point where Man United can say, "Okay, this is the striker we want."

"Zirkzee was wanted by Juventus. Zirkzee was wanted by Fiorentina over the summer transfer window. I will not be surprised to see Italian clubs returning and jumping again on Joshua Zirkzee in the January transfer window, because there's always been interest in Zirkzee from Italy after he did fantastic at Bologna and then he joined Manchester United.

"For Zirkzee, there was also an opportunity at Everton in the final minutes of the summer transfer window, but it didn't happen because of one reason: the deal collapsing, also with Monaco and that Balogun story at the end of the summer window. So what's the situation now?

"Joshua Zirkzee is going to have a conversation with Mauricio Pochettino. Joshua Zirkzee is doing his best with Man United, and he's described as one of the best professionals at Manchester United. Always training at the best level, always doing his best for the team. But at the same time, Zirkzee wants to play.

"Zirkzee has wanted to go and play for some time now, not only in the recent weeks or months; Zirkzee wants to go because he wants to play. He loves Man United, but he feels he's not a regular starter, and he wants to play football. He wants to play regular football.

"So let's see what kind of opportunities will arrive on the table. But I will not be surprised to see Joshua Zirkzee on the move in January, unless Mauricio Pochettino can sort the situation with the boy and clarify the situation."

While it's clear that Zirkzee wasn't in the plans of Michael Carrick at Old Trafford, it remains to be seen if Pochettino has the same feeling with him.

The Netherlands international had a strong pre-season before being sidelined by Carrick, but he has scored twice in his last four appearances for the club, all coming off the substitutes bench, against Como and Aston Villa.

His technical qualities are unmatched in the squad, and if Pochettino is capable of getting him to link with the rest of the forwards in the squad, then he could be a really useful member of the squad. But if he doesn't want to be at the club, then there is no point keeping him around.

With that said, Man Utd's squad is far too thin right now, and they cannot afford to let him leave in January without replacing him first. It's imperative that any forward signing is brought in before a move for Zirkzee is sanctioned to ensure they're not left short, and the club will now have the chance to make that happen for the new manager as he looks to revolutionise Man Utd.

This season’s Premier League title race may be locked in a paralysed state of uncertainty but Arsenal, the defending champions, are determined to keep it interesting.

While the painful delay on Manchester City’s battle against their guilty verdict threatens to drag deep into next year, Arsenal are remaining hot on their tails.

City’s lead at the top is back to three points but Arsenal’s win here was unlikely to have sent any shivers down the spines of Enzo Maresca and his players in this phoney mess of a season.

It was not until the 80th minute that Arsenal finally registered their first shot on target, and that was the moment which ended their cycle of frustration at the City Ground.

Just when it appeared Mikel Arteta was heading for a third successive goalless draw at the home of Nottingham Forest, substitute Noni Madueke’s deflected strike proved the difference.

Noni Madueke breaks the deadlock at the City Ground! 🔓 https://t.co/RdL48f3OLC

Trips to the City Ground have rarely been easy for Arsenal, with an FA Cup defeat in January 2022, at a time when Forest were still in the Championship, sparking a famous Arteta rant in the dressing room which was included in the All Or Nothing documentary.

They were far from fluent here and have now failed to score in the first half of their last six Premier League and Champions League matches.

Eberechi Eze endured a particularly difficult afternoon in what was a missed opportunity for the England international, with Madueke replacing him at half-time. Yet Arteta will argue that finding a way to win games when not at their best is a sign of champions.

“We have played 11 competitive matches and won 10 of them, we are in a good place and will improve,” Arteta said. “Since losing at Brighton we have won three games in a row so that is the response that I want.

“The level of the league has gone up again and there will be more and more surprises. We have to go again at Bayern Munich this week [in the Champions League on Wednesday night] and we will have to adapt to that one too.

“I have a smile on my face as Noni is a special guy. He’s in a good moment and after the [international] break he’s shown another level. The team needs him and he’s doing well.”

Arsenal often struggled against teams who operate with a compact midfield and defend deeply last season and this was another case in point.

Delap’s shot from a tight angle is then deflected wide. Forest corner, from which Murillo’s header loops into Raya’s gloves. Forest showing more attacking ambition.

Liam Delap is producing a very decent centre-forward performance.

The £50m record signing is proving a real threat with his power and running.

Madueke and Rice not one the same wavelength, before Delap does well to win a shoulder to shoulder with Gabriel only to slice his cross behind for an Arsenal goal kick. Sums up the lack of attacking quality in the game.

Forest have another free-kick in a shooting position after Havertz is penalised for blocking a long shot with his hand. McAtee’s effort from the free-kick is scooped miles over the bar.

Both teams looking livelier in the early exchanges of the half, but Forest’s counter-attack was the more dangerous, with Liam Delap doing well to hold on to the ball and whipping a cross into the box that was just ahead of Williams.

Noni Madueke replaces Eberechi Eze, so a more natural wide player on his stronger foot on Arsenal’s left flank.

Frustrating first half for Arsenal and Mikel Arteta will be demanding more from his attacking players.

Arsenal have not registered a shot on target so far and their delivery from set-pieces has been poor.

Forest look relatively comfortable and had the best chance of the half with a shot from Dan Ndoye which was saved by David Raya.

Are we heading for a hat-trick of 0-0 draws at the City Ground between these two teams?

A very uneventful 45 minutes which has been played at the pace of a pre-season game at times. Similarities with the last two fixtures between these teams at the City Ground, and Arsenal’s games against Leeds and Lille this week. They put their foot on the pedal after half-time in both games, and they need to do the same here.

Guimaraes is off the pitch, and there will be more than two minutes added now as a result of his treatment. Forest win a corner, but Havertz heads away at the near post.

Just the two minutes of added time to play.

Liam Delap wins a free-kick in a shooting position for Forest after Arsenal were caught with numbers forward. Big moment for the home team, this. Calafiori was caught on the ball again, he has not had the best of games.

Williams and McAtee are over the free keek, which is around 25 yards out, left of centre.

Williams blasts the ball into Bruno Guimaraes, who goes down and stays down after taking the shot flush in the face.

More incisive from Arsenal, with Rice punching the ball into Odegaard and then on to Havertz but the angle was always against him and the German could only shoot into the side-netting. Forest have defended very well, overall. Although they have been deep for the most part, they have jumped and pushed out at the right times to stop Arsenal accessing the box.

Glasner and Arteta dish out some instruction while there is a stoppage in play to deal with a hand in the face that troubled Schlager. Can either side find a breakthrough before the break?

David Raya claimed that Forest corner with ease and the game has now resumed its pattern. Forest retreating into their shape, and Arsenal passing in front of them. Schlager penalised for a foul on Saka, the home fans not happy with the decision, I think because Saka was going away from goal.

Rice clips in a menacing delivery, but Havertz skewed his header wide from seven or eight yards. Good chance, Arsenal’s best so far.

More Arsenal probing but the small details are letting them down: Eze’s return to Odegaard forced his team-mate to check, and then Odegaard’s touch was heavy after a wall pass from Guimaraes.

Delap does well to make a nuisance of himself at the other end, and his long-range shot deflects behind for a corner.

Strong from Konsa to win the ball, drive out of defence and win a foul. Rice with a well-weighted scoop over the Forest defence for the run of Ben White, but he skewed his cross behind for a goal kick.

Arsenal with another corner. No doubt they have been the game’s dominant force when it comes to possession and territory, but there has been a lack of cutting edge so far. Saka goes for the near post again but Forest deal with it. The home crowd groan at Sels for not releasing the ball quickly in search of a break.

Arsenal work the ball across their midfield with Guimaraes, Rice and Odegaard all involved, and a dangerous Saka cross is headed behind for a corner.

Scramble! The near-post flick on caused chaos and Konsa’s goal-bound backheel was blocked, but the ball would not quite drop for Ben White to score a tap-in.

After two successive goalless draws here between the two clubs, this is following a similar script so far.

It’s a very tight affair with Arsenal enjoying more of the possession but Forest seemingly happy with that and content to them on the break.

Bruno Guimaraes has made a bright start for the visitors.

Forest’s best attacking moment of the game and it comes from an Arsenal mistake.

Calafiori just had to play a five-yard pass back to Gabriel but scuffed it, and Munoz pounced. Running at the Arsenal penalty area, Munoz’s cross was deflected to the back post and the ball found it’s way to Ndoye. Decent reverse shot through legs, but Raya had it covered and tipped around the post.

From the corner, Forest are penalised for a foul.

Arsenal continue to have Forest penned in their own half, very difficult for the home team to play through the midfield or over Konsa and Gabriel so far.

Saka produces his first successful dribble to beat Williams, and the left wing-back trips him at the expense of a free-kick and a booking. Rice’s delivery from the right was uncharacteristically poor.

Munoz tries to drag Forest up the pitch to apply some pressure on Arsenal but he is penalised for a shirt pull on Gabriel. The atmosphere sounds pretty sleepy, a result of some tepid Arsenal possession and Forest’s bad home record.

Forest making sure they have numbers around Saka whenever Arsenal funnel attacks down their right, which is almost always their preferred side.

Neat from Guimaraes in midfield to turn and find Saka with some earlier service, and Sels tips his cross away from danger.

Delap and Ndoye waiting for a slip-up or counter-attack but they are feeding on scraps at the moment. Arsenal yet to carve out a proper chance, though.

It’s already pretty clear that one of the key duels today will be between Gabriel and Liam Delap.

Forest’s record signing Delap has already let Gabriel know he’s in the game with his physicality.

Cute pass from Bruno Guimaraes to break the Forest midfield line and find Odegaard, but strangely the Arsenal captain could not sort his feet out to control the ball and back a clean pass. Then Williams defends well against Saka from an Arsenal attacking transition.

Pretty subdued start from Forest. The crowd’s spirits were raised there by Delap chasing down Konsa who had the deal with the sun his eyes, but the Forest striker pushed him in the back.

Arsenal enjoying all of the possession so far, and most of it has come in Forest’s half. One or two players on Arsenal’s right/Forest’s left struggling with the low evening sun. Havertz did get in behind but his cross into the middle was too strong.

Arsenal get the game under way, and play short from kick-off.

There will be a degree of pressure on birthday boy James McAtee today to make an impression.

With Morgan Gibbs-White injured, McAtee is likely to take the No 10 position and continue his redemption arc.

McAtee has been revitalised since the arrival of Oliver Glasner and this is a big afternoon for the former England under 21 international.

In honour of nine-year-old Forest fan James Kerry, who died earlier this month of cancer.

We'll wear black armbands this afternoon, as we join our hosts in remembering nine-year-old Nottingham Forest supporter, James Kerry, who passed away earlier this month following a brave battle with cancer. Rest in peace, James ❤️ https://t.co/YFIXnCfJJX

Surely we cannot have another 0-0 in this fixture? Looking at the talent in Arsenal’s front third, and the fact they are playing their two most offensive full-backs, this might be more open than assummed.

Arsenal can cut Manchester City’s lead to three points with a win today but does it all matter?

Manchester City’s battle against their guilty verdict is threatening to run into next year and this title race feels fake and damaged.

It is a sham of a season with the prospect of asterisks all over the Premier League campaign.

Arsenal can only carry on as normal as they defend their title but this is an unsatisfactory mess.

The margins are really small and it’s a team and a manager that we know really well, extraordinary manager, really well organised.

They are dangerous in many areas, a very well set-up team and you need to be very tight, very neat, very efficient in everything that you do. You have to insist and insist, and then there’s a lot of volume of actions.

[On coming from behind] Yes, and it’s part of the game, your capacity when something doesn’t go as planned to react and still win the game, and we know the challenge that we have here. In the last two years, we haven’t been able to win here and that’s an opportunity as well to show what we are made of.

Another reason Arsenal will be feeling confident today is Forest’s abysmal home form in the Premier League.

It may surprise neutrals outside of Nottingham but results at the City Ground have been poor for some time.

Indeed, it is just two league wins in 11 months in front of their own supporters which, quite frankly, is relegation form.

Before this game, Forest’s head coach Oliver Glasner said: “We have to change it. I spoke to one or two experienced lads who know Forest better than I do and talked about the situation. But if you always talk about the problem it makes it bigger and bigger.

“We haven’t scored a goal at home yet or won a game at home, and that is what we have to change.”

Trips to the City Ground have seldom been easy for Mikel Arteta, with two successive 0-0 draws in the Premier League.

An FA Cup defeat in Jan 2022, at a time when Forest were still in the Championship, sparked a famous Arteta rant in the dressing room which was included in the All Or Nothing documentary.

Yet Arsenal have secured two wins in a row since that defeat at Brighton, without being truly at their fluent best, and will be confident against a Forest team without injured talisman Morgan Gibbs-White.

Dominguez and Schlager are the preferred midfield pair in the 3-4-2-1 with Sangare on the bench. McAtee and Ndoye will support Liam Delap in attack. Much attacking responsibility on Munoz at right wing-back, who also has the cavalier Calafiori on his side of the pitch, which could prove fireworks.

No surprise that Havertz, Odegaard, Saka and Calafiori are restored to Arsenal’s Premier League starting XI having started on the bench in mid-week. Eze over Madueke and Guimaraes over Lewis-Skelly were closer calls for Arteta. Ben White comes in for Timber, with Arsenal managing the minutes of both right-backs.

Fascinating stuff from Sam Dean this morning, who has profiled a member of Mikel Arteta’s inner circle who is not listed on Arsenal’s website. Germán Castaños, an expert in innovation who has written multiple books on alternative thinking, has become a key member of the team. Things started with a phone call with Nicolas Jover, then a meeting with Arteta and now he splits his time between Argentina and London. Find out more about Arsenal’s mystery man and his methods here.

In the ordinary course of a Premier League season, you would say Manchester City have applied pressure on Arsenal by opening up a six-point lead before the champions play at Nottingham Forest this afternoon.

This is not a normal Premier League season though, and we await to discover if the top of the league table is simply a mirage.

Regardless, Mikel Arteta and his Arsenal players have their own motivations to accumulate as many points as possible before January as they seek to retain the title for the first time since the 1930s.

Arsenal have struggled at the City Ground, drawing 0-0 on their last two Premier League visits. They also lost at Forest in May 2023, a result which confirmed Manchester City as champions at Arsenal’s expense, and were knocked out of the FA Cup by Forest in January 2022.

Forest are yet to score a home league goal under Oliver Glasner, another data point suggesting this will be a low-scoring game.

That might not be the full story though, with Forest creating a hatful of chances in their defeat at Crystal Palace last week and Arsenal also playing a more inventive, technical game with the ball so far this season.

Arsenal have yet to score from a non-penalty set-piece, and their percentage of goals from open play is now the highest in the Premier League.

Morgan Gibbs-White is a doubt after sustaining what Glasner described as a “minor muscle injury” at Palace and his involvement in the game will be a last-minute call. With the exception of Christos Tzolis, Piero Hincapie and long-term absentee William Saliba, Arsenal’s squad is in pretty good health. Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard, Kai Havertz, Riccardo Calafiori and Ben White could be recalled to Arteta’s starting XI after starting the Champions League win over Lille on the bench.

#1305. Kean: Como and Italy striker’s return from injury delayed

Multiple sources in Italy say Moise Kean’s return to action with Como has been delayed due to a new tibia issue.

Italy and Como striker Kean will be out longer than expected.

The 26-year-old last played in October, featuring in Italy’s 1-1 draw against France, and was expected to miss five weeks.

However, La Provincia di Como and Sky Sport Italia claim that Kean will need more time to recover.

According to La Provincia di Como, Kean recently saw a new specialist, while Sky claims the striker has developed new problems in his tibia.

Sky confirms Kean’s recent specialist visit, adding that it took place in Barcelona in the past few days.

Although the nature of his new problem remains unclear, Kean won’t be back anytime soon, as both media outlets say the ex-Fiorentina and Juventus star needs more time to return to action.

Kean joined Como from Fiorentina in a €40m deal last summer. The Italy international scored one goal and provided one assist in six appearances before his injury.

#1304. Tim Howard Names ‘Brilliant’ Manager USA Have to Hire Instead of Pep Guardiola

Former USMNT goalkeeper Tim Howard has named the 'brilliant' manager he'd love to see replace Mauricio Pochettino, going as far as to claim he would be a better fit for the USA than Pep Guardiola.

That's quite the statement from the 47-year-old, considering the Spaniard's glittering CV. Guardiola has lifted six Premier League titles during his time at Manchester City, while also collecting three Champions League crowns across spells with City and Barcelona.

When it comes to the greatest managers in world football, few can hold a candle to him, and he remains the highest-ranked among those still active in the game.

But Howard, who earned 121 caps for his country, isn't convinced Guardiola would be the 'right fit' for a USA side boasting the likes of Folarin Balogun, Antonee Robinson and Christian Pulisic. Instead, he's thrown a major curveball by backing a very different candidate, with his choice likely to raise more than a few eyebrows.

Howard has caused a huge uproar after advocating for his former Everton manager, Roberto Martinez, to be the next USMNT coach. He was speaking to Landon Donovan on the Unfiltered Soccer podcast about possible new coaches for the USMNT. “Roberto Martinez, he's the most brilliant football mind I've ever been around,” Howard said.

“So I would say this, and I hope people at U.S. Soccer will hear this. I honestly, hand on heart, think you're absolutely absurd, U.S. Soccer, if he is not your top one or two candidates. Do not pass Roberto Martínez by. Please don't. U.S Soccer, whether it's Dan [Helfrich] or JT [Baton] or Gooch [Oguchi Onyewu], all the guys I know, please.

He has got to be top two candidates. And for me he's one. “Think about this. He took Wigan, by the way, Wigan were a bunch of farmers. Like Wigan were terrible. They were terrible. He got them to over 500 passes in games on average, won the FA Cup against Manchester City. Okay? I know they got relegated. He then comes to Everton. We were a Moyes Everton team, and we had a blueprint, and it worked and it was successful. He came to us and changed our entire identity. Our identity before was really good, sure. He just changed it and made us different."

Zlatan Ibrahimovic isn't a fan of the manager put forward to replace Mauricio Pochettino as the next USMNT manager.

He continued: “His ability to teach players to get tactical. His ability to get tactical awareness from players. At Everton, let’s say you're his best right-winger. If you can't do it, he’ll get the second best guy and that player will thrive in his system, which will make you better because you don’t want to lose your place. He's just brilliant.

“Oh, then by the way, he coached two massive national teams, Belgium with their golden generation, big players, and Portugal. And by the way, he handled Ronaldo. And if anyone thinks Ronaldo's easy to handle, ask their most recent manager. He guided it expertly. He knows World Cups. He knows club football. He knows players. It's a no-brainer for me. And you can see by the way I'm speaking.”

Howard and Martínez worked together at Everton from 2013 to 2016. The Spaniard started off his managerial career in Wales with Swansea, and worked for English clubs like Wigan and Everton.

He then coached Belgium in the 2018 and 2022 World Cups, and Euro 2020. He won them their first ever third place medal in the 2018 World Cup, but notably failed to get the best out of the country's golden generation, with the likes of a prime Kevin De Bruyne and Romelu Lukaku seemingly destined for silverware.

U.S. Soccer have high expectations for whoever steps into the role recently vacated by the Argentine

The 53-year-old coached Portugal in the 2026 World Cup, and helped them win the Nations League over his home country Spain in 2025. But whether he really ranks among the top coaches remains up for debate - he is heavily criticised because his possession-heavy style often feels slow, overly cautious, and unable to turn elite talent into decisive wins in major tournaments.

He also often seems to lack a 'Plan B', which means rivals find it easy to read his next move. That's a far cry from Pochettino's reign, as the new Red Devils boss is excellent at finding new ways of getting the best out of his team, making him a smart long-term project manager.
